title: ASCRIBE-XR: Extended Reality for Visualization of Scientific Images
problem: Scientific data visualization from experiments, particularly 3D dense arrays and mesh files, is challenging at scale. Traditional tools lack immersive exploration, multi-user collaboration, and integration with remote HPC resources.
motivation: Immersive visualization enables scientists to better understand complex 3D data structures and patterns. Integration with HPC for remote processing and multi-user WebRTC-based collaboration can accelerate research and enable distributed teams.
method: ASCRIBE-XR is a VR application built on Godot engine integrating: (1) local VR rendering for immersive exploration, (2) HPC integration for remote large-scale data processing with streaming results, (3) WebRTC+MQTT multi-user capabilities for real-time collaborative visualization.
key_novelty: System-level integration of VR, HPC, and AI-driven object modeling for scientific visualization with multi-user collaboration support.
contributions: VR platform for immersive 3D dense array and mesh visualization
HPC integration enabling remote processing of large-scale data with streaming to VR
Multi-user real-time collaboration via WebRTC and MQTT
Integration of AI-driven object modeling for automated feature detection
Godot-based implementation for cross-platform VR support
limitations: Abstract provides limited technical performance details; no comparison with traditional visualization tools; scalability limits not discussed.
primary_theme: Immersive scientific visualization and HPC integration
